chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Ismail (peace be upon him) buried his mother in Al-Hijr, and built a chamber upon it, lest the grave of the mother of Ismail (peace be upon him) be trampled upon in Al-Hijr.

key_terms.الْحِجْر: Al-Hijr: The semi-circular walled area near the Kaaba, also known as Hijr Ismail.
key_terms.حَجَّرَ: He built a wall/chamber: Refers to constructing a boundary or enclosure.
key_terms.يُوطَأَ: Be trampled: To be walked upon or stepped on, often referring to the feet of pilgrims.

ai.seo_question: Where was Hagar buried and how was her grave protected according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the reverence of the Imams for the sanctity of the graves of prophets and their families, specifically noting that Ismail (as) built a low wall (hijr) around Hagar's grave to preserve it from the foot traffic of pilgrims. This historical detail provides the etymological and physical basis for the term 'Hijr Ismail' in the Kaaba, which remains a significant part of the prayer area during Tawaf. It underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition in maintaining the dignity of the deceased within the sacred precincts.
